notes: ENTERABLE landmark, UNCHANGED footprint/door/stair. Round tapered plaster tower (8 m base -> 6.4 m at 21 m), 6 storeys of 3.4 m (floors at z 0.2/3.6/7.0/10.4/13.8/17.2), flat roof with the projecting gallery band at 20.3 m, and a 6 m round lantern drum rising through the roof to 24.6 m under a conical metal cap (tip ~26.8 m). ONE way in: timber door on the s face, centre 0, 1.1 x 2.1 m, sill 0; interior floor_z 0.2. Stair is AUTHORED: five flights of 16 risers x 0.2125 m (tread 0.24, run 3.84 m, width 0.95) along y from y +1.9 (foot, 1.6 m inside the door) to y -1.9, rising away from the door; flights alternate x +0.625 (flights 1,3,5) and x -0.625 (2,4). The top storey opens up into the lantern drum (glazing 21.7-23.5 m on four faces). REVISION: windows cut from 15 to 7 (three small glazed windows stacked on the s face at sills 4.7/11.5/18.3 + the four lantern lights) and the base/mid string courses dropped, keeping only the gallery band - Mason's walk gate fails any GLB over 16 surfaces and every glazed pane is one surface; the old spec compiled to 26. A lighthouse tower is near-blind in reality, so this reads more correctly anyway. Round plan -> ~8k collision-shell tris: accepted for the one landmark, per mason.md.

ENTERABLE, two ways out, UNCHANGED footprint/doors/stair. Front door s face centre 0 (1.2 x 2.2 m, timber); back-yard door n face centre -4.0 (1.0 x 2.1 m). Interior floor_z 0.2, 2 storeys of 3.2 m (floors at z 0.2 and 3.4). Stair: explicit, enclosed stair hall hard against the WEST wall (x -6.55..-5.45), run along y from y +2.9 (foot, nearest the front door) to y -1.3 (top), 16 risers of 0.20 m, rises away from the front door; the enclosure's own doorway faces the front wall with 1.5 m of standing room. Ground floor: everything east of x -5.4 is open; the back band y -4.55..-1.5 x x -3..+6.5 (3 x 9.5 m) is clear for the bar and a seated regular. Mason has no rooms/partition key, so UPSTAIRS is one open floor (13.1 x 9.1 m) with the stairwell + newel rail at the west end; furnish it as three rooms with prop partitions (suggested party walls at x -2.5 and x +2.5, corridor along the n wall). Two stone chimney stacks on the gable ends (e at y +1.5, w at y -1.5), now capless solid masses fused into the body. Slate gable, ridge along x, 3.0 m rise; plinth course only (string course and eaves band dropped - on a multi-part building every band is a collision-shell solid and the door cutters split the plinth ring in two). REVISION for the 16-surface gate: glazed windows cut from 25 to 7, all on the STREET front: 4 ground (+-2.4, +-4.4, sill 0.9) + 3 upper (-4.4, 0, +4.4, sill 4.3). The rear (n) windows - ground +2.5 and upper -1.5/+1.5/+4.5 - are BLIND niches (0.2 m recess, solid inside: the n wall is plain from inside on both floors; the bar band along it needs its own lamps). Gable ends blank, as on a real Cornish inn. Surfaces: body/roof/trim + 2 leaves + 7 panes + shell (body, roof, 2 plinth arcs) = 16.

Furnish with stalls/fish boxes between the piers; leave the three s bays open.

SEALED (floors:1, no interior). L-plan stone farmhouse built as TWO gabled ranges rather than plan:{shape:L}: Mason clips ONE gable to an L plan, which leaves the wing under a sheared-off roof edge, whereas two ranges give a proper cross-gable with a valley. Main range 12 x 6 along x at the rear (y -5..+1), slate gable ridge along x; wing 5 x 7.5 projecting forward on the west (x -6..-1, y -2.5..+5), ridge along y, both 5.8 m eaves / 2.6 m rise, overlapping 3.5 m so they fuse. Bounding box exactly [12, 10]. Blind niche door (1.0 x 2.05, 0.12 m recess) on the WING's s face at wing-centre +1.6 (= model x -1.9), i.e. in the re-entrant angle beside the main range's front wall (which sits 4 m behind the wing's front). Two stone chimney stacks (capless solids to 9.0 m): e gable of the main range (x +5.55, y -2.0) and the wing's front gable (x -3.5, y +4.55). 9 glazed windows: wing front -1.0 (ground + upper), wing w face ground +1.5, main front 1.0/4.0 (ground + upper), main rear upper +-3.0 (16 surfaces: 3 visual + 9 panes + shell body, roof, fused plinth, fused cornice).

SEALED landmark (floors:1, no interior; every opening `glass:false` - a derelict shell). Cornish beam-engine house on the moor: stone house mass 6 x 10 m (offset to x -1.0), 12.0 m to the eaves under a slate gable with the ridge along y (ridge 14.6 m), 0.6 m walls, heavy plinth to 0.8 m and a string course at 8.2 m. Two rows of tall narrow windows on the w flank (sills 3.0 and 8.6 at +-2.5) and on the e flank where the stack does not cover it (+2.5), a big arched opening on the n gable (1.6 m, crown 4.8) and a small one above. Everything fits the [8, 10] footprint exactly (house x -4..+2, stack x +1..+4). Round plan is spent only here, as the one moor landmark. Surfaces: body + roof + trim + shell (~6) - no panes.

SEALED (floors:1, no interior). Lifeboat house: stone, 5.5 m eaves, steep slate gable ridge along y (3.0 m rise) so the 8 m gable end faces the sea (s). Big double boat-door BLIND NICHE on s centre 0, 2.6 x 3.0 m, 0.3 m recess (no leaf, no gate flag needed - a niche is exempt from the door gate). Small arched glazed window over the doors (sill 3.6, crown 4.7) and three glazed 0.9 x 1.2 windows at sill 2.6 on each flank (e/w at -3, 0, +3) = 7 panes. Plinth + eaves cornice (top-level). Timber-and-stone read comes from the slate roof + timber door leaf colour in the niche; Mason parts cannot stack a timber upper storey on a stone base (every part starts at z 0).
